subject: Re: Just Called - Private AI leaders Dinner in Bellevue
text:
1. What are you most excited about personally or professionally regarding
AI?

Professionally. Agentic engineering and verifiability: defining the right
abstractions for what the system should be, what must remain immutable
without human input, what should be able to be mutable & even
autoregenerated on demand or rebuilt, & how systems can be restructured
into composable task-oriented primitives where workflows/dataflows can
easily be created or restructured as needed, with AI in the loop, +
autogenerated UIs for humans in the loop.

2. What do you see as the biggest gap in AI implementations so far?
 1) The learning curve - because people presume that it understands
english, that you can build ad-hoc
 2) Most companies have already put robust automated verification systems
and automated operability, allowing hundreds of humans to push to prod
daily with automatic monitoring and rollback on regression. Much of what is
needed to make AI a net positive, and not a liability relies on this level
of engineering practice and discipline, and they aren't there without AI
let alone with AI. Since AI, like any automation amplifies outcomes, this
needs to be dialed in. Most engineers or companies don't even think this
way, let alone have it's practice dialed in for years, to be able to tweak
it in an AI context.
3) Organizational bureaucracy—the tax of middle management and
coordination—is the biggest bottleneck, not necessarily engineering. Thus
gains from AI without reshaping the organization is often minimal
4) Hype and FUD confusing things. People just wanting to "purchase" a
solution, rather than putting in the hard effort to make it work

3. Any dietary restrictions? We'll pass this along to the restaurant.
No.

subject: Re: Great Meeting!
text:
Colin, Laura,

It was a pleasure speaking with you both, and apologies for the delayed
follow-up — I blame Vegas :)

Thanks again for sharing the walkthrough of your audio editor. I've shared
it with our team and we'll keep it in mind as our needs for data annotation
and labeling evolve.

I also wanted to share more about our audio separation services and check
whether you've heard any feedback from the audio customers you mentioned.
Based on our discussions, a few capabilities seem like they could be
particularly useful for customers on your platform:

   - *Multi-speaker separation:* splitting a single file with multiple
   speakers into one clean track per speaker, isolated across the full stream
   including overlapping sections.
   - *Speech isolation:* removing background noise from recordings captured
   in imperfect environments. This demo
   <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zkEMM2Uh2WQ> showcases both
   multi-speaker separation and speech isolation, and this one
   <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=310UK1s3DvY> highlights the downstream
   transcription accuracy improvements speech isolation can deliver.
   - *Music removal:* stripping copyrighted background audio from streams
   where it would otherwise limit licensability. Demo here
   <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ce3mw78hzK4>.

We regularly work with data providers, aggregators, and data services
companies to apply our models to mixed audio, producing clean isolated
tracks from content that would otherwise be difficult to use for training,
or just hard to understand and transcribe.

I'd love to chat further if any of this could plug into Encord workflows.

Best,

Krista
